newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end up for second straight record.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end up for second straight record.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed up, hitting a second straight record as bullish sentiment from Venezuela's ongoing oil auctions continued to infect equities.
But traders warned profit-taking could set in Thursday.

"There's been strong demand from abroad, mainly stemming from the oil auction ... But prices are up now and it's not out of mind to think there could be an adjustment tommorrow," said Banesco broker Simon Brad.
The bolsa's 19-share index rose 1.53 percent to end at 7,150.19 points, as 61 million share traded worth 12 billion bolivars ($24 million).
Merinvest's composite index, which includes telephone company CANTV, meanwhile closed up 1.11 percent at 114.20 points.
Brad said other good news included May's 3.1 inflation figure, released late Tuesday, "which was above government forecasts, but below many market estimates."

Among traded issues, 28 rose, 13 fell and five closed flat with pulp and paper company Venepal A shares leading gainers to rise 7.43 percent to 115.00 bolivars. Venepal is due to release second quarter figures later this week.
